linkedin:
Scan a signed QR code on an AuthiChain-registered product and your phone's own camera app opens authichain.com/verify — no separate app to install, no login. The page reads a product ID and a cryptographic hash straight out of the QR data, checks the hash, and returns one of three plain-language states: Authentic Product Verified, a Counterfeit Alert with an explanation of what failed, or Product Found — No Hash Signature, when the item is on the registry but the scan didn't carry a signature to check.

Underneath the badge sits the product card itself — name, brand, manufacturer, serial number, category, and the date the item was registered — so the person holding the product sees what's actually on file, not just a checkmark. It's SHA-256 verification under the hood, and the page states its own status plainly rather than dressing an unverified scan up as a pass.

We think the right test for a customer-facing verification page isn't how it looks — it's whether someone who's never heard of QR signing schemes can read the result and trust it.

https://authichain.com/verify?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=consumer-verify-flow&utm_content=a

reddit.title: What a customer sees after scanning our product QR — a three-state plain-language verify page, no app required
reddit.body:
AuthiChain issues signed QR codes for physical products. Scanning one opens authichain.com/verify with the product ID and a cryptographic hash encoded in the URL — no app to install, it just opens in whatever camera/QR reader the phone already has.

The page checks the hash against what's on file and returns one of three states: Authentic Product Verified, a Counterfeit Alert (with the specific reason the hash didn't check out), or Product Found — No Hash Signature, for items that are registered but the scan didn't carry a signature to verify. Below that badge is the actual product record — name, brand, manufacturer, serial number, category, registration date — so the shopper sees the data, not just a badge.

Question for people who've built customer-facing authenticity pages: how much do you show below the pass/fail badge? We landed on showing the full record, on the theory that a bare checkmark asks for blind trust, but I'd like to hear where others draw that line.

https://authichain.com/verify?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=consumer-verify-flow&utm_content=a

Disclosure: I work on this project.
